findings.evidence: ParityOdd.lean:75 is `public section` (Basic.lean:82 is `@[expose] public section`, which is why `kWit` needs no such lemmas); the author's use of `(rfl)` at lines 374/376 confirms the body is unexposed.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp] lemma kFour_k : kFour.k = ![0, 0, 0, 1] := (rfl)` and the same for `kFour_kPrime` and `kFour_pPrime`.
findings.issue: `kFour` is a 5-field `DisKinematics` under a plain `public section` (line 75, no `@[expose]`), but only `kFour_p` and `kFour_q` accessors are given (lines 374, 376). `kFour.k`, `kFour.kPrime` and `kFour.pPrime` cannot be reduced by any consumer outside the module, so the witness kinematics cannot be used on the lepton side at all (Layer 1 contracts `L^{μν}W_{μν}` on exactly these).

findings.evidence: ParityOdd.lean:421 uses `bilinMap_apply_left_eq_zero _ ![K.p, K.q] 1 v` (index 1 = `q`) only; index 0 is never used. The leptonic twin exposes all four as `@[simp]` (Basic.lean:294-311: `lMuNuOdd_apply_k_left_eq_zero`, `_kPrime_left_eq_zero`, `_k_right_eq_zero`, `_kPrime_right_eq_zero`).
findings.fix: Add `@[simp]` lemmas `aFour_apply_p_left_eq_zero`/`_right_eq_zero` (and the `q` right form), each a one-liner: `AlternatingMap.bilinMap_apply_left_eq_zero _ ![K.p, K.q] 0 w` and `..._right_eq_zero _ ![K.p, K.q] 0 v`.
findings.issue: `aFour K` has no lemma for `aFour K K.p w = 0` or `aFour K v K.p = 0`, and the `q` right-slot form only comes via `ParityOddAssumptions.conserved_right`. The roadmap lists "antisymmetry, annihilation of `p` and `q`" as the properties `A` must carry (README line 134); for general `K` a consumer must unfold `aFour_eq_det` to get the `p` ones (`aFour_apply` is `kFour`-specific).

findings.evidence: Basic.lean:576 `.smul`, 582 `.sub`, 589 `.flip` — no `.add`; ParityOdd.lean:115 `smul` is the only algebraic closure lemma on `ParityOddAssumptions`, and ParityOdd.lean:126 proves the zero case inline rather than via a reusable lemma.
findings.fix: Add `IsProperLorentzCovariant.add` (and `.neg`, `.zero`) beside the existing `.sub`, and `ParityOddAssumptions.add`/`.neg`/`.sub` beside `.smul`.
findings.issue: Closure API is lopsided: `IsProperLorentzCovariant` gets `.smul`, `.sub`, `.flip` but no `.add` (or `.neg`/`.zero`), and `ParityOddAssumptions` gets `.smul` plus `parityOddAssumptions_zero` but no `.add`/`.sub`/`.neg`. The results assert the parity-odd tensors are a one-dimensional span, i.e. a submodule, and the remaining Layer 0.2 headline (`(W₁, W₂, W₃)` assemble to a tensor injectively) needs addition of the three structures; a consumer must currently route `.add` through `.sub` of a `(-1) • W` rewrite.

summary: The headline surface is right — `A` enters as data with its properties, bodies stay unexposed, and the spectator-frame structures are extensional. Three interface gaps: `kFour`'s lepton fields are unreachable, `aFour` lacks the p-annihilation lemmas the roadmap requires of `A`, and the closure lemmas for `IsProperLorentzCovariant`/`ParityOddAssumptions` are lopsided.
